title: OpenMuCF muon-cost ledger row
description: One published/derived muon-production energy cost, carrying its full accounting basis and provenance. Each row of data/muon_cost.csv must satisfy this. This is a curated compilation with provenance, not an evaluation: every OURS-normalization step is shown verbatim in 'derivation', facility rows are original derivations labeled 'implied, derived here', and no accounting credit (e.g. recapture) is ever silently folded in. A cost is only meaningful as a POINT ON A 2-D GRID of 'stage' (how far along the produce -> capture -> transport -> moderate -> stop-useful-in-D-T chain the muon has got) by 'numeraire' (the units the energy is counted in: beam kinetic, or electrical on one of two facility denominators). Wall-plug is a numeraire, NOT a stage. 'basis_class' is the deprecated 1-D predecessor of 'stage' and is retained as an alias. Values at different (stage, numeraire) coordinates are NOT commensurable: cross-coordinate aggregation is not meaningful and the generator must disclose it.

citation.description: Human-readable source citation (public: by author/venue/DOI, never by acquisition route).

tier.description: T1 = purpose-built muon-source design studies; T2 = demonstrated technology (e.g. muon-collider front end, collected-not-stopped); T3 = operating facilities (GeV/stopped-mu is OUR derivation, no facility reports it).

basis_as_published.description: The quantity as the source states it (per pi-, per created mu, per stopped mu, per collected mu; beam vs wall-plug). The normalized value lives in normalized_GeV_per_mu, at THAT ROW'S OWN (stage, numeraire) coordinate -- there is no single common basis; this records what the source actually reports.

recapture_credit_applied.description: True iff an accounting recapture/breeding credit is folded into normalized_GeV_per_mu. Kelly's x2.5, which his abstract attributes to recapturing waste-particle kinetic energy and generating heat through tritium breeding, is such a credit and is kept SEPARATE (applied=false, factor in recapture_factor); a credit is never silently folded into the normalized value.

recapture_factor.description: The recapture/breeding credit factor if the source quotes one (e.g. Kelly x2.5, stated in his abstract); recorded even when recapture_credit_applied=false, so the credit is visible but not folded in. Empty if none.

eta_acc_assumption.description: Accelerator (electricity -> beam kinetic energy) efficiency the source assumes, if stated (e.g. Kelly 0.18, rounded from the PSI HIPA measurement). Dividing by it is a NUMERAIRE change (beam_kinetic -> electrical_*), not a stage advance: it converts the units the energy is counted in and applies no collection, moderation or stopping correction. Kept separate, never folded into a beam_kinetic row. Empty if the source does not state one.

eta_mu_assumption.description: The fraction of PRODUCED mu- the source assumes are actually delivered to the D-T vessel -- i.e. the whole capture + transport + moderate + stop segment collapsed into a single factor. Recorded exactly like recapture_factor and eta_acc_assumption: visible, but NEVER folded into normalized_GeV_per_mu. How well-founded it is lives in eta_mu_evidence_status, and that is what decides whether it may be composed at all. Empty if the source states none.

eta_mu_evidence_status.description: evidence_status of eta_mu_assumption specifically (same enum, same meanings). Kelly, Hart & Rose state they do not know eta_mu and adopt an 'arbitrary but reasonable assumption' of 50%, so their factor is author_declared_arbitrary: it may be DISPLAYED, but composing it yields a BOUND that must never be rendered as a value nor enter a headline. Empty where the row states no eta_mu.

value_as_published.description: The verbatim published value + unit (kept as text because sources report heterogeneous quantities).

normalized_GeV_per_mu.description: Energy per muon in GeV at THIS ROW'S OWN (stage, numeraire) coordinate. The name's 'normalized' means normalized to per-muon, NOT normalized to a common basis: the rows mix per-produced, per-transported, per-stopped-useful-in-D-T and per-stopped-in-another-target figures, and they are now counted in two different kinds of energy (beam kinetic and electrical). Values at different (stage, numeraire) coordinates are NOT commensurable and must never be aggregated silently -- in particular a tier median is only meaningful within one numeraire. Empty ONLY for a needs_verification row whose digit is not pinned.

numeraire.description: The UNITS normalized_GeV_per_mu is counted in. Wall-plug is a NUMERAIRE, not a stage: the eta_acc conversion is a change of units applicable at ANY stage, so modelling it as a sequential node would make 'electrical energy per TRANSPORTED muon' inexpressible without re-applying eta_acc downstream. 'beam_kinetic' = beam kinetic energy delivered by the accelerator. 'electrical_minimal' = electrical energy on the minimally-required-subsystem denominator (PSI HIPA grid-to-beam 18.3%: 1.3 MW beam / 7.12 MW of only those subsystem parts needed to produce the beam). 'electrical_site' = electrical energy on the facility's total draw (PSI HIPA 1.3 MW beam / 12.5 MW site = 10.4%). Both electrical variants are defensible and come from the SAME primary on two different denominators; that is why the numeraire must be carried per row rather than assumed. Empty only on an unpinned needs_verification row.
numeraire.$comment: Both PSI HIPA denominators: Kovach, Parfenova, Grillenberger & Seidel, J. Phys. Conf. Ser. 874 (2017) 012058, abstract + section 4.

stage.description: How far along the muon chain this cost is counted, following the five verbs by which the muCF cycle-closure literature defines the muon cost: produce, capture, transport, moderate, and stop one USEFUL negative muon in the target. The muCF chain is produced -> captured -> transported -> moderated -> stopped_useful_in_dt; only that terminal stage is the quantity a muCF energy balance actually needs, and every earlier stage is a LOWER BOUND on it because each omitted conversion factor is <= 1. 'stopped_other_target' is a non-D-T sink (e.g. an aluminium stopping target): it is NOT a point on the muCF chain, no chain of sub-unity factors connects it to a muCF cost, and it is not a bound on one; it is still carried in its tier and read by aggregates over that tier. Empty only on an unpinned needs_verification row.
stage.$comment: Supersedes basis_class; the mapping is documented in that field's description.

evidence_status.description: How well-founded this row's number is. 'primary' = read from the source's own text/table/figure; 'primary_cited' = the source states it and attributes it to a primary that has itself been read; 'derived_here' = OUR arithmetic on published inputs, shown verbatim in derivation; 'author_declared_arbitrary' = the source itself calls the value arbitrary or unknown; 'assumption' = assumed without the source saying so; 'absent' = the quantity is simply not in the literature. The last three are NOT SOURCED: any figure that composes one is a BOUND, never a value, and must never headline.

useful_fraction_sourced.description: Only meaningful when stage='stopped_useful_in_dt'. True iff the source establishes that the muons it counts are USEFUL in the cycle-closure sense (actually available to catalyse fusion), rather than merely stopped somewhere in the fuel. False marks a row that maps onto the terminal stage but whose 'useful' qualifier its source never establishes -- such a row is still a bound, not a value. Empty where the stage is not the terminal one.

basis_class.description: DEPRECATED ALIAS of 'stage', retained because downstream code and the public MUON_COST.md text still refer to it; do not delete it, and keep it consistent with 'stage'. Mapping: produced -> produced; collected -> transported; stopped_in_dt -> stopped_useful_in_dt (with useful_fraction_sourced recording whether the source actually establishes the 'useful' qualifier, which for every row held today it does NOT); stopped_other_target -> stopped_other_target. The alias is 1-D and cannot express the numeraire axis, which is precisely why 'stage' + 'numeraire' supersede it. Empty is allowed only on an unpinned needs_verification row.

charge_basis.description: Which muon charge the figure counts. muCF needs mu-; 'mixed' counts mu+ and mu- together (so the mu--only cost is higher by a factor this ledger does not source) and 'mu_plus_only' is irrelevant to muCF and must never enter a muCF cost aggregate -- any statistic this ledger forms over rows: a tier median, a spread, a ratio, or the edge of a prior box drawn over a tier. That is a different bar from the stage rule above: an aggregate is a statistic over a tier's rows and may contain a row that is not itself a point on the muCF chain. Empty only on an unpinned nv row.

derivation.description: Every OURS-normalization step VERBATIM: 'implied, derived here: <formula with numbers>' for facility/derived rows; 'as-published; no OURS-normalization' where the row is copied straight from the source.

needs_verification.description: True iff the muon-cost digit is not pinned from the primary text (paywalled/not in hand). A needs_verification row may never headline anything.
